annotationRationale: The solution tests composition in both orders using coordinate rules for translation, reflection, rotation, and dilation. The quarter-turn rule is derived from the specified rotation direction and angle, using cnm_244 to identify corresponding points. The composition node is used for composition only, without iteration.
sourceMethod: Follows the official coordinate calculation for all six pairs, organizing the comparisons in a table and briefly deriving the quarter-turn coordinate rule.

review.mathCheck: Independently verified all six pairs. TF, RD and FD agree in both orders, yielding (x+2,-y), (-2y,2x) and (2x,-2y). TR and TD disagree at the origin; RF disagrees at (1,0). Thus exactly 3 pairs commute, choice C, matching the key. The every-point requirement correctly handles exceptional points where noncommuting transformations may agree.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA Solution 13 on pages 6 and 7: identical coordinate rules and exhaustive comparison of both orders. The added quarter-turn derivation and composition-order explanation make the method reconstructible at AMC 10 level. The official L-shaped illustration is supplementary and unnecessary to this argument.
review.annotationCheck: All five assessed concepts are directly used. Composition is assessed without iteration; ordinary coordinate arithmetic is background. No material omission, incorrect direct node or replacement is needed.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The four exact links support the displayed coordinate translation, axis reflection, rotation correspondence and origin-centered homothety steps. Broader construction and property criteria are not all assessed. Composition and commutativity have no supplied CN alignment, so national coverage is incomplete.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 8.G.A.3 supports the translation, reflection and dilation coordinate rules; 6.NS.C.6b supports reflection signs. G-CO.A.4 supports the rotation-definition aspect used, without demonstrating definition development. The accepted partial G-CO.A.2 link is exercised through point-function representation, without distance/angle comparison. The quarter-turn rule is derived locally. Homothety's partial links to G-SRT.A.1, G-SRT.A.1a, G-SRT.A.1b, G-SRT.A.2, G-SRT.A.3, 8.G.A.4 and G-C.A.1 do not demonstrate experimental dilation properties, segment-length verification, similarity criteria, AA derivation or circle similarity here. No supplied link covers commutativity.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All immediate nodes fit: math:function-composition-iteration for composition order and equality; cnm_086 for translation coordinates; cnm_136 for axis reflection; cnm_244 for finding the specified quarter-turn image; cnm_275 for coordinate dilation. Unused portions of their criteria are not claimed as assessed.
